sources.name: RDF 1.1 N-Quads
sources.role: Line-based UTF-8 RDF dataset serialization, default/named graph term, quad statement and media-type contract
verified_facts: N-Quads is a line-based plain-text syntax for encoding an RDF dataset.
Its syntax extends the N-Triples style so a statement may include a fourth graph-label term.
The registered media type is application/n-quads and the character encoding is UTF-8.
semantic_limits: Successful N-Quads parsing establishes syntax-to-dataset conversion, not source authority, completeness or physical truth.
A graph-label IRI or blank node is dataset structure and must not be reused as cadastral parcel identity or source provenance.

Dataset-equivalent quads do not prove equality of downloaded bytes, and numeric literals must not become parcel-height evidence without exact source, geometry, CRS, vertical datum, units, method and execution receipts.

sources.name: RDF 1.1 XML Syntax
sources.role: RDF/XML document grammar, namespace/base/language resolution, node/property element and XML-to-RDF graph mapping contract
verified_facts: RDF 1.1 XML Syntax defines an XML syntax whose grammar actions generate triples in an RDF graph.
The syntax uses XML namespaces and supports node elements, property elements, resource references and typed literals.
XML base and language information can affect the IRIs and literal language tags produced by parsing.
semantic_limits: A well-formed RDF/XML document and successful graph construction do not prove that its assertions are authoritative or physically correct.
Equivalent RDF graphs or XML trees do not establish equality of original source bytes, transport completeness or immutable publication identity.
A typed numeric literal remains a graph assertion and must not become a terrain measurement without exact source object, parcel geometry, CRS, vertical datum, units, algorithm and execution receipts.

sources.name: SPARQL 1.1 Federated Query
sources.role: SERVICE graph pattern, remote endpoint execution, variable endpoint, SERVICE SILENT and federated solution-join contract
verified_facts: SPARQL 1.1 Federated Query defines the SERVICE graph pattern for executing part of a query against a remote SPARQL endpoint.
A SERVICE target can be an IRI or, in permitted cases, a variable bound to an endpoint IRI.
SERVICE SILENT suppresses service errors and substitutes a neutral solution behavior instead of failing the whole query.
semantic_limits: A successful remote SERVICE call proves endpoint evaluation, not source authority, completeness, freshness or physical truth.
Federated results depend on remote endpoint state, query planning and time; they are not an immutable source snapshot unless exact requests, responses and digests are pinned.

SERVICE SILENT can mask remote failures, so returned bindings or numeric literals must not create parcel-height rows without explicit endpoint and source-object receipts plus geometry and measurement evidence.

sources.name: SPARQL 1.1 Query Results CSV and TSV Formats
sources.role: SELECT result-table transmission, CSV lossy RDF-term rendering, TSV RDF-term syntax, charset and row/column serialization contract
verified_facts: The Recommendation defines CSV and TSV formats for expressing SPARQL SELECT query results.
CSV is a lossy encoding that renders result terms as strings without preserving every RDF-term distinction.
TSV encodes RDF terms using SPARQL/Turtle-style syntax and requires a header row of variables.
semantic_limits: A correctly serialized result table proves formatting of query solutions, not authority or completeness of the underlying source dataset.
CSV can lose datatype, language, IRI, literal and blank-node distinctions, so reconstructed values must not be treated as exact RDF evidence.

A numeric CSV or TSV field is query output rather than a measurement receipt and must not become parcel-height evidence without source bytes, exact polygon, CRS, vertical datum, units, method and execution receipts.
